solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Don't change way in which core is removed

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle, so its middle letters go

parts.note: a street is a way, as in road names
the two central letters of STREET are taken out

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave some method alone after a heart has been taken out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is the proofreader's mark meaning 'let it stand', written beside a correction that should be ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is Latin for 'let it stand', telling a printer not to change the text.

clue.text: Award-winning picture: Selfie with His Majesty?

definitions.meaning: the 1956 musical film won five Oscars
a selfie shows me, and here the king is in it too

explanation.surface: A prize-winning photo that turns out to be someone posing beside the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' wants to be a photograph, which the selfie supports; it is a film. The question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The King and I is a film, and films are pictures that win awards.

clue.text: Chunter on about club

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone muttering endlessly about their golf or social club.
explanation.walkthrough: To chunter is British for to grumble under your breath. 'About' reads as 'on the subject of', but it is shaking up the nine letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short heavy club carried by British police officers.

clue.text: A danger VAT put off artistic pioneers

indicators.note: put off can mean disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: Experimental artists deterred by the threat of a sales tax on their work.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the UK's sales tax, which makes 'put off' read as discouraged; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The avant-garde are the artists who push ahead of the mainstream.

clue.text: Three articles Penny found in soldier's quarters

parts.note: AN, THE and A are all articles
p = penny

explanation.surface: A soldier's barracks where someone turned up three items and a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is the soldier ant, a worker caste that defends the nest, so its quarters are an ant heap rather than a barracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldier ants live in the nest, so an ant heap is where a soldier is quartered.

clue.text: Hubris in sailor just the start of navy's awful, awful year

definitions.note: Latin phrase for a dreadful year, made famous by the Queen in 1992

indicators.note: the first awful says the letters of hubris, in, sailor and the navy letter make an awful mess, rearranged
just the start of navy's is its first letter

parts.note: navy's gives its opening letter only

explanation.surface: A sailor's arrogance at the outset of a naval career leads to a terrible twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'awful' is the trick: the first is the anagram signal, the second belongs to the definition. 'just the start of' navy's gives N; HUBRIS, IN, SAILOR and N together are rearranged into the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Annus horribilis is Latin for horrible year, famously used by Elizabeth II of 1992.

clue.text: Work in that place is cause of death

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: there = in that place
op = opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A warning that working somewhere will kill you.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'work' a job that kills you; it is a single musical piece. 'The rope' is the hangman's noose, as in 'facing the rope'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rope means hanging, so it is the cause of death for the condemned.

clue.text: Aggressive Trump broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out as sound, so the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: to ruff is to play a trump card in bridge or whist

explanation.surface: A news report on an aggressive Donald Trump.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes Trump the president; he is a card-game verb. RUFF and ROUGH are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough play is aggressive play, as in a rough tackle.

clue.text: Arrive in middle of Manhattan, out of cash at first

indicators.note: out of means without, so a letter is removed
only the first letter of cash is meant

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, fitting Manhattan
the first letter of cash, which is taken out

explanation.surface: Turning up in midtown New York with no money at the start of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Manhattan is there to say the middle should be spelt the American way, CENTER, so that removing C leaves ENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: coming into a room or a city is arriving there.

clue.text: Hesitancy spoilt ANC lecture

indicators.note: a spoilt thing has been damaged out of its proper form

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A nervous speaker ruins a talk to the African National Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: The ANC is South Africa's governing party, but here its letters are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctance is unwillingness to act, which is hesitancy.

clue.text: Old writer's lines thrown out. Time to give up?

parts.note: QUILL, an old pen, loses LL (lines)
t = time

explanation.surface: An aging author whose verses were rejected wonders whether to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old writer' is a pen, not an author. L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: quitting smoking or a job means abandoning it, which is giving up.

clue.text: Learner infiltrating enchanter's group

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside

parts.note: Circe, the enchantress of the Odyssey
L = learner, from L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee sneaking into a wizard's coven.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's joins the wordplay to the definition, so 'group' is not owned by the enchanter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a social set of friends or colleagues is called their circle.

clue.text: Footwear from the east nearly here — it's quite something

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, backwards

parts.note: Crocs are a brand of chunky rubber clogs

indicators.note: nearly means the word stops just short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone notes that some shoes from the Orient have almost arrived, and they are impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reverses CROCS to SCORC, and 'nearly' cuts HERE to HER. Crocs are moulded plastic clogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorcher is informal for something remarkable, such as a stunning goal or a very hot day.

clue.text: Project to repeal tax abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

parts.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: A government scheme to scrap a tax has been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' reads as a noun, a scheme, but the answer is the verb: to project a trend forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to project known figures forward to estimate what comes next.

clue.text: Villa guest nursing a fever

indicators.note: nursing means holding, so the answer is held inside the words

parts.note: villA GUEst

explanation.surface: A holiday visitor at a villa laid up with a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' fits the sick guest so well that it hides its job of holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits.

clue.text: Bent on tipsy rep being sacked

definitions.note: a bent is a natural inclination, a noun

indicators.note: being sacked here means being plundered and wrecked, so the letters of on tipsy rep are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tipsy sales rep, fond of drink, is fired from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like an adjective, crooked, but here it is a noun: a natural leaning. 'being sacked' scrambles ON TIPSY REP.
explanation.definitionFit: A propensity is a tendency or inclination, the same as having a bent for something.

clue.text: What's lost in era of the psychiatrist?

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Asking what has been forgotten in the age of therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in reverse clue order: the psychiatrist first, then the era. Shrinkage is the retail word for stock lost to theft or damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the amount lost, as in stock that goes missing from a shop.

clue.text: Dull Republican trapped in loveless marriage worked for CIA?

parts.note: UNION without O

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a CIA agent spies
R = Republican, placed inside SPIED

explanation.surface: A boring politician stuck in a cold marriage turns out to have been a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' reads as a cold relationship; it strips the O out, since love is zero in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninspired means lacking spark, which is dull.

clue.text: Disrespectful of a European academic to take precedence

indicators.note: to take precedence is to go first, so this piece is placed at the front

parts.note: prof = professor
an is the form of the article a before a vowel
E = European

explanation.surface: Complaining that a professor from Europe insists on going first.
explanation.walkthrough: The academic is written last but told to go in front. The article 'a' becomes its other form, since the next letter is a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane means showing disrespect for sacred things.

clue.text: Idle cop took drugs, boss finally admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the boss's letter goes inside

parts.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
to have used is slang for having taken drugs

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of boss

parts.note: boss gives its last letter, S

explanation.surface: A lazy police officer has been on drugs, his superior having finally confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the last letter of boss ('finally'), is 'admitted' between DI and USED. DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something idle in the sense of disused is no longer in operation, like an idle factory.

clue.text: Outspoken radical examined

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a red is a political radical

explanation.surface: A blunt revolutionary has been scrutinized.
explanation.walkthrough: The past tense READ is said like RED. 'Outspoken' looks like it describes the radical.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going through a report closely is studying, or examining, it.

clue.text: A few ticks and I'll be off

definitions.meaning: reads as the British 'in a tick', a moment; meant as the literal ticks of a clock mechanism
reads as leaving; meant as exploding, the way an alarm or a charge goes off

explanation.surface: Someone saying they will leave in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The speaker is a device counting down with a clockwork timer, and when the ticking stops it detonates.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue is spoken by the device: its clock ticks for a while, then it explodes.

clue.text: Scandalous information circulating about American gang

indicators.note: going round, so the word turns back on itself
about means around, so this word surrounds the next

parts.note: dirt is scandal, as in digging up dirt
A = American, placed inside the turned word

explanation.surface: Gossip going round about an American criminal outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes between TRI and D. A triad is a Chinese criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese organized-crime gang.

clue.text: Money matters

definitions.meaning: wealth, as in a person who lives beyond their resources
a verb: is important to someone, as in 'your friendship ___ a lot'

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it is a heading about finance; split, it is a noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Means is wealth, and to mean something to someone is to matter to them.

clue.text: High-ranking gentleman from Ibiza controlling island

indicators.note: to control something is to hold it, so this word holds the next

parts.note: señor is Spanish for gentleman, and Ibiza is Spanish
I = island, placed inside SENOR

explanation.surface: An important Spanish man who is in charge of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibiza is there only to make the gentleman Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior means higher in rank.

clue.text: Country queen giving one new position

indicators.note: the letter I (one) is moved to a new place in the word

parts.note: a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: A rural monarch promoting someone to a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for the queen, as in country house; it is the definition. Only the one letter I moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Iran is one country among many, the Middle Eastern state once called Persia.

clue.text: Crafty individual, likely to go far in the main?

definitions.meaning: a seaman works on a craft, and 'able' is skilful

definitions.text: likely to go far in the main?
definitions.meaning: the main is the open sea, where sailors travel far

explanation.surface: A cunning person who is tipped to succeed, on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' means cunning but also 'of boats', and 'in the main' means mostly but also on the high seas. An able seaman is a navy rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An able seaman is a trained sailor, a person on a craft who sails far across the main.

clue.text: Not happy place is charging sick

indicators.note: to charge something is to load it, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: diseased = sick
PL = place, as in street names

explanation.surface: An unhappy patient complaining that the clinic bills them for being ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charging' sounds like billing; it means loading, as a gun is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone annoyed or dissatisfied is not happy.

clue.text: Always back party shunning right wing

indicators.note: the right-hand end of the word is avoided, so its last letter goes
back means backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a revel is a party
the right-hand end of REVEL, which is shunned

explanation.surface: A loyal member who keeps supporting a party that has turned its back on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'right wing' make a political picture; the party is a celebration and the right wing is the end letter of REVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always, as in 'ever faithful'.
